discovery: Photonic crystals: the photonic band gap concept and its realization in photonic crystal fibers

nominees.name: Philip St.J. Russell
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for the Science of Light, Erlangen, Germany

motivation: In 1987 Yablonovitch and John independently proposed that periodic dielectric structures could open a photonic band gap: a frequency range in which light cannot propagate. Yablonovitch showed this would suppress spontaneous emission, and John showed it would strongly localize photons. Yablonovitch then built the first three-dimensional photonic band gap material. Russell carried the idea into optical fibers. Beginning in 1996, his photonic crystal fibers, including hollow-core fibers that guide light in air by a band gap, gave physicists unprecedented control over dispersion, nonlinearity and confinement. These fibers made possible the supercontinuum sources essential to the self-referenced frequency combs behind the 2005 Nobel Prize. Photonic crystals turned the band theory of electrons into a design principle for light. Today they underpin nanocavity quantum optics, low-threshold lasers, topological photonics and new fiber technologies. This is a fundamental physical insight that has become a universal platform for controlling light at the wavelength scale.
